What the numbers mean

Pick tower · 3 levels

Levels 1 & 2: active pick locations feeding the conveyor.
Level 3: approximately 10 pack stations distributed beside the conveyor.
Shared outbound flow: conveyor weighing scales and automated print-and-apply, then the common route to the downlanes. Floor VAS remains in front of the tower.

Level roles and equipment presence are user-confirmed. Exact station positions, equipment quantities, elevations and transfer mechanisms remain illustrative. Weighing and labeling counters record passages only; weight values, pass/fail tests and processing times are not modeled.

Model boundary

Custom JavaScript process model and Three.js reconstruction. Geometry and richer equipment meshes are adapted from your supplied Claude model; robot controls, scenario provenance and comparison tools extend the portfolio version.

CAD trace and zone placement are source-derived. Scale, heights, equipment footprints, dock identifiers, exact connections and travel paths have not been independently surveyed. Collision avoidance is only demonstrated at the Locus bridge.

Four Stretch robots are reported; only three active dock positions are located. Lane 7 is exceptions / international / parcels, not an assumed seventh retail lane. No synthetic Lane 7 volume is assigned.

Fixed scenario assumptions

Staging / docks12 north doors × 26 pallets; 4 manual inbound positions; 66 shared receiving positions. Unverified.
WorkstationsApproximately 10 pack stations on Level 3, reported by the user; exact placements are illustrative. 2 floor VAS, 2 high-volume customer process stations and 6 chargers remain unverified.
Handling40 s high-rack lift; 20 s low handling; VNA pick 240 s; 30 s case induction; 30 s downlane pickup. Demonstration values.
Other processingWrapper 60/90 s; VAS 360–600 s; High-volume customer three 150 s stops; 60 s outbound load/pallet; 8-pallet minimum after a 3 h cutoff. Demonstration rules.
Demand / missions4–7 Locus stops/mission; pick 0.7–1.4× entered time; pack 0.6–1.5× entered time; 82% inbound reserve routing. Synthetic demand and inventory.
Reliability / batteryExponential Stretch intervention interval; repair 0.5–1.6× entered duration. Battery drain 0.55/0.15 percentage points per min; charge 1.6 points/min; thresholds 25/95%. Unverified.
Travel / inventoryModel units, not surveyed feet; conveyor base 2–2.3 units/s × multiplier. Synthetic rack occupancy; no SKU-level inventory, LWH or orders.

No shift calendar is assumed. Runs use elapsed scenario time. Known masterpack, slotting, top-40 Specialty and unslotted-wave rules remain in the separate Inputs & rules case-study model; this task-level demonstration does not claim to enforce them.

Before decision use

Replace every operating assumption with WMS / time-study inputs, validate scale and routes, reconcile inventory and order identities, model queues and safety logic, and run replicated experiments against observed site behavior. One illustrative run has no statistical confidence interval.
